Definition: middle voice from G4253 and G5087; to place before, i.e. (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine):--purpose, set forth.
BiblicalUsage: Protithemai means to set before, to exhibit, to purpose. God set forth Christ to be a propitiation through faith in His blood. He made known unto us the mystery of His will, according to His good pleasure which He hath purposed in Himself. And Paul says he often purposed to come to Rome, but was let hitherto.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God set Christ before the world as the mercy seat, the place where His wrath and His love meet. I hold that the same God who purposed redemption in Himself also purposes my steps, and even Paul's hindered journey was inside that purpose.
